title: RF Telemetry System
subtitle: Evolving a 2.4 GHz RF link-evaluation platform into an LR2021-based 915 MHz / 2.4 GHz flight telemetry subsystem with RF-health monitoring and hardware-first protection
stackup: The existing evaluation-board implementation is four layers; the stackup for the LR2021 flight revision is still being finalized
summary: An avionics RF project that began as a 2.4 GHz link-characterization board and is now being developed into a dual-band LR2021 flight telemetry subsystem. The current architecture combines a CM5 telemetry supervisor, 915 MHz and 2.4 GHz half-duplex RF paths, external PA/LNA/filter stages, antenna diversity, forward/reflected power sensing, system-health telemetry, and hardware paths that can force unsafe RF states off independently of Linux software.
keyComponents: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 telemetry supervisor
External PA, LNA, and band-selective filter chains
Directional couplers for forward and reflected RF sampling
RF T/R and antenna-diversity switch network
Comparator and eFuse-based hardware shutdown paths
mainConstraints: Maintain controlled-impedance RF paths and continuous reference planes through a dense mixed-signal layout
Never hot-switch a high-power RF path; PA/LNA states must be safely sequenced around RF-switch transitions
Protect the PA and RF power tree from overtemperature, overcurrent, and severe antenna mismatch
Preserve observability of RF power, reflected power, temperature, current, voltage, and fault state
Do not make Linux software the only layer capable of placing the RF front end in a safe state
Support both a robust long-range 915 MHz mode and a higher-rate 2.4 GHz mode through one supervised radio architecture
publicNote: This page intentionally separates architecture decisions, design targets, and measured results. RF output power, final switch/filter losses, thermal limits, component selections, and the LR2021 revision stackup remain preliminary until hardware validation is complete.
